description: Exercise O-read-response-identity with two distinct remote origins: lose all contextual heartbeats for A, admit B, then deliver genuine B quorum confirmation and observe response identity for both removed requests. B is an in-history comparison, not a different obligation.

harness.description: Three real Peers, test LogDB, bootstrap/election/persistence/application handoffs, then fixed selective heartbeat loss and FIFO delivery; inspect admitted statuses and resulting messages/readiness.
semantic_changes: No target code changed. Memory storage is used without crashes; deterministic transport send-loss policy and abstract bootstrap/noop application replace outer layers.
All observations occur synchronously between calls; no concurrency, sleeps, termination or private protocol state injection.

legality.derivation: Three real Peer instances use Launch(initial=true,newNode=true) with identical three-voter bootstrap addresses and NewTestLogDB. Bootstrap entries and every later update are appended and state saved before messages are scheduled, then Peer.Commit completes the handoff. The abstract application consumes actual committed bootstrap configuration entries through ApplyConfigChange and the empty election noop, then NotifyRaftLastApplied reports actual consumed indexes; there are no user writes. Tick only node 1 until natural election and drain all resulting messages. Require every peer knows leader 1, shares its term and has applied the committed current-term noop. ReadIndex on peer 2 generates and forwards A; its two actual contextual heartbeat sends fail by declared policy. All other messages, including B from peer 3 and genuine heartbeat responses, use one global FIFO queue, a stricter schedule than per-link FIFO. Source Transport.send permits individual failed sends (including full queue) and NodeHost.sendMessage does not resend failures; no Unreachable event is required for that path. Fixed contexts are legal nonzero outputs of the production context domain, not injected confirmations. After forwarded B is handled, observe both pending statuses before processing its heartbeats. Drain remaining messages through Peer.Handle and all update completions. Memory storage substitutes durability without crashes; no network/worker resources exist. No private raft mutation or test-only election override is used.
legality.applicability: Single-threaded no-crash Peer integration harness, unchanged membership; substitutes a permitted lossy transport and synchronous abstract application for bootstrap/noop only.
unresolved: No real transport queue saturation or client RequestState timeout is executed; these are scope limits, not observed outcomes.
alternatives: No arbitrary message reordering is required. Persisting before all outgoing messages is a permitted slower schedule than early replication.

grounding.derivation: Use accepted O-read-response-identity. Response signatures concatenate actual destination and both context words, one per emitted response to the independently identified origin. The prerequisite expected signature is formed from actual admitted readStatus.from/ctx before confirmation; result is formed from actual Peer.GetUpdate messages. Two distinct origins make association independent of the compared context. A released request implies exact one-response identity, while an unreleased request does not test the duty.
grounding.applicability: Stable-term leader consumes the admitted pending remote read after genuine follower heartbeat acknowledgments.
alternatives: Higher released index is permitted and not compared.
No client completion deadline or full application value is checked.

observable_properties.description: For each independently identified admitted origin whose pending request was removed, the actual response destination/context signature must equal its admitted destination/context signature. Both context words and multiplicity are compared.

uncertainties: This is local response-correlation, not a client deadline or global linearizability measurement.
A non-release would make this implication hold without testing emission; actual release is recorded separately.
